chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Bobby Troup: the perfect job
summary: Collins left Sinatra for Bobby Troup's trio for five years, doing all the playing, and got studio work around Hollywood.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: That's right, it's just, you know. It was no comparison, you know. But Nat and Sinatra, they are giants, you know, musically. So during this time, as I said, I worked with Sinatra, and I was -- at this time I was also working with a very dear friend of mine, Bobby Troupe. Now, Bobby -- I said to Bobby, look, I'm going to go with Sinatra. I said, John, go and stay, three months, four months, doesn't make any difference. When you're ready to come back just come back.

Bobby Troupe is a very -- as you know he's a very talented man, and he's a very prolific writer. He's a Phi Beta Kappa, right. And he is an actor. But he's primarily a writer now. This was the perfect job for me. I joined Bobby after I joined Nat. Now, this was the perfect job for

me in that Bobby played piano, but not too much piano. He wanted to get up and sing and stand up, so consequently I had to do all the playing. So I got a chance to be the accompanist, the soloist, and I stayed with Bobby for about five years, and really got it together. You know. So consequently everybody around Hollywood starting becoming aware of me, and I got an awful lot of recordings, and started doing quite a bit of studio work, you know. I had a few shows and this, you know.

But that was the perfect job and the perfect situation because Bobby is a beautiful person. And he loves musicians, he admires musicians, he respects musicians, and it's -- everybody loves him. All the guitarists would come in. I would go to work one night and here's Howard Roberts, John Gray, they all would come in and we would play and really get some kicks. And Bobby loved guitarists too, as you know. So that was a very good job for me at that time, because I got my chops together --
